source_lines.29: In the positive-characteristic nondegenerate level-one regime, the normalized cellular head dotD(lambda) for each restricted partition lambda is isomorphic, with shift zero, to the normalized simple of the same right crystal label lambda. The reduction J(lambda) of the characteristic-zero normalized simple contains that crystal-labelled simple once, and has no constituents with cellular labels not dominated by lambda. Its G0 class is invariant under finite-module diagram duality. This proves the CP label comparison needed for the crystal-labelled adjustment matrix; it is not a positive-characteristic global-basis identification.

source_lines.27: For a nonzero finite-dimensional standard homogeneous cyclotomic KLR module M over any field, choose a word by successive maximal last-color blocks i_1^{r_1}...i_s^{r_s}. Among the simple shift orbits occurring as constituents of M, exactly one normalized orbit S_c contributes to that word; its right crystal label is c=tilde f_{i_s}^{r_s}...tilde f_{i_1}^{r_1}u_Lambda. Its word graded dimension is product_a [r_a]_{i_a}!, and [M:S_c]_v equals gdim e(word)M divided by that product. All other simple orbits occurring in M have zero space at this word; simple orbits absent from M may have nonzero space there. The zero module has zero character and requires no extremal-word selection. Consequently graded word characters are injective on G0. If two fields have modules with the same word character, their extremal words and detected canonical B(Lambda) labels coincide. No one-dimensional word-space assertion is made. Choice is inherited only through the existing abstract crystal identification.
source_lines.39: 1.1 Let M be a nonzero finite-dimensional standard homogeneous cyclotomic module. Choose a nonzero word by successively maximizing the last constant-color block, then the preceding block after restricting that maximum, until the vacuum is reached. Write the resulting word as i_1^{r_1}...i_s^{r_s}, adjacent colors distinct. Restriction to a word idempotent is exact. Every simple constituent of M with nonzero word space must have precisely the same first maximal last-block length: a shorter length gives zero, a longer length would contradict maximality for M. The actual maximal-tail supplier identifies the full maximal restriction of this simple with N tensor L(i_s^{r_s}), where N is simple with zero residual i_s-tail. Repeat on N and on the corresponding exact restriction of M. At the end N is the unique vacuum simple. Reconstruct using the actual unique-head induction supplier. Hence exactly one simple shift orbit among the constituents of M can contribute at the chosen word. Its crystal label is obtained by the same successive right-induction powers from the vacuum, so is field independent under the native11 canonical B(Lambda) identification. [F1, F2, algebra]
source_lines.41: 2.1 For the normalized simple S in that orbit, maximal restriction is normalized N tensor normalized L(i^r): restriction commutes with finite vector duality, the two factors are absolutely simple, and their unique self-dual normalizations force the remaining shift to be zero. The normalized rank-r nil-Hecke simple has graded dimension [r]_i!, by the actual polynomial/corner calculation with shift -d_i binomial(r,2). Iterating gives gdim e(word)S=product_a [r_a]_{i_a}!. Therefore the coefficient of [S] in [M] is gdim e(word)M divided by this nonzero product. [F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra]
